audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI put claims are missing from the common-equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $74.171 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.19 per diluted share and 3.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The put settlements are claims against common equity that bypass owner earnings through equity adjustments; the bridge includes no RNCI claim or corresponding acquisition of minority earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, redeemable noncontrolling interests ("RNCI") consist of interests in consolidated subsidiaries for which the Company has entered into separate option contracts by which the Company has the right to purchase the remaining non-controlling interests through a call option and the non-controlling interest holder has the right to sell the non-controlling interest to the Company through a put option.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission from the bridge is demonstrated. The latest filed RNCI balance alone exceeds the difference between the $30.31 bear value and the $30.35 market price, so it can change a scenario conclusion. The $74.171 million is only a scale comparison: actual formula-priced settlements and the value of minority earnings acquired remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year and forecast to earnings attributable to existing common holders, calculate each remaining put's formula value and exercise timing, and rerun the bridge and OE forecast consistently.

audit_findings.title: The preferential Puerto Rico tax regime expires inside the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.206 million 2025 tax-rate reconciliation benefit from income subject to the exemption grant, equal to 35.6% of the $135.4 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration without renewal would increase recurring income, property and municipal taxes, reducing forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, if Evertec Group fails to renew or extend the decree, all preferential tax benefits will expire on December 31, 2026 for income tax purposes, December 31, 2027 and June 30, 2028 for property and municipal license tax obligations respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Expiration dates are filed facts, while renewal remains unresolved in the supplied record. The filed 2025 tax benefit is large relative to anchor OE, and most Puerto Rico taxable income receives the 4% rate; loss of the regime is therefore reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the executed renewal decree or current agency disposition, identify its effective dates and rates, and rerun explicit and terminal taxes under both confirmed-renewal and expiration cases.

audit_findings.title: Dimensa creates a mixed earnings and balance-sheet perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $199.317 million purchase price, $179.757 million net acquisition cash outflow and $184.538 million new long-term debt proceeds; purchase price equals 9.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 OE anchor excludes Dimensa and its acquisition financing, while the June 2026 cash and liability bridge is post-close; acquired OE and incremental interest therefore do not share the bridge perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the terms of, and subject to the conditions specified in, the SPA, Evertec BR will purchase all outstanding common shares of Dimensa from the Seller for an aggregate purchase price of approximately R$ 950 million (the “Transaction”), representing approximately USD $ 184 million at current exchange rates, subject to customary adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated dating and perimeter error: Dimensa closed April 30, 2026, not during FY2025. Excluding Dimensa earnings understates value, while omitting the acquisition-funded debt's interest from the historical anchor can overstate value under an equity-OE method that does not deduct debt. The net direction depends on Dimensa's sustainable OE relative to financing costs.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the April 30 closing, consideration and financing, derive Dimensa OE from filed post-close results or supportable standalone statements, include incremental interest and reinvestment, and rerun on one consistent post-close perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Major Popular contract cliffs are absent from the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $270.2 million of 2025 revenue was attributable to Popular, computed as 29% of $931.818 million; contract-specific OE loss is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The existing discount and possible renewal concessions or lost services affect OE growth, while the 2028 and 2030 expirations occur before the terminal period and can alter terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The A&R MSA, A&R ISO Agreement, and A&R BPPR ATH Agreement have terms ending in 2028, 2035, and 2030, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The contract expirations and customer concentration are demonstrated, although renewal outcomes are unresolved. A customer representing 29% of 2025 revenue is sufficiently large that non-renewal or material concessions are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion; smooth growth and an unchanged terminal base do not address that exposure.
audit_findings.action: Allocate Popular revenue and contribution profit among the MSA, ATH and ISO agreements, annualize the existing 10% discount, and rerun explicit renewal, concession and non-renewal cases at each contractual date.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include operating, trapped or minority-owned cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $260.659 million added to equity value, or $4.20 per diluted share and 12.0% of base equity value; $226.3 million, or 86.8%, resides outside Puerto Rico
audit_findings.mechanism: Only surplus cash attributable and distributable to existing common holders belongs in the bridge; operating, settlement, restricted, acquisition-committed, taxed or minority-owned balances do not.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $306.0 million, of which $263.7 million resides in our subsidiaries located outside of Puerto Rico for purposes of (i) funding the respective subsidiary’s current business operations and (ii) funding potential future investment outside of Puerto Rico.
audit_findings.explanation: The full add-back is demonstrated, but the non-surplus portion is unresolved. The filing states that most cash funds subsidiary operations or investment and may face distribution restrictions and taxes. Because the add-back is $4.20 per share, classification could materially change the scenario range and margin-of-safety threshold.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a legal-entity cash schedule separating settlement and minimum operating cash, restrictions, committed uses, repatriation taxes and RNCI ownership; rerun the bridge using only verified surplus common-equity cash.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may retain non-operating R&D tax-credit gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.9 million in 2025 and $8.9 million in 2024, totaling $21.8 million; the 2025 amount equals 9.5% of the $135.4 million anchor, but the valuation effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, non-operating tax-credit gains inflate historical OE and the log-trend anchor used to project explicit and terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, other income , net is primarily comprised of a $ 12.9 million net gain in research and development tax credits in Puerto Rico, $ 2.3 million in realized gains on foreign currency transactions, a $ 0.2 million gain on sale of investments and a $ 0.1 million realized gain for change in fair market value.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains and their non-operating, multi-year nature are demonstrated, but the supplied OE reconciliation does not establish whether they were retained. Their scale could matter, yet the effect on the fitted anchor cannot be established without tracing the OE calculation; this remains an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Trace other income through each historical OE calculation, identify all tax-credit and investment gains, document any recurrence and required reinvestment, and rerun the trend after removing unsupported non-operating amounts.
